target: Eu insisto que ele está errado.
english: I insist that he's wrong.
old: 'Insistir que' + indicative when asserting a belief/fact.
focus: Give the contrast: insistir que + indicative asserts a fact; subjunctive would turn it into a demand for action.

target: Aqui é raiz, não tem frescura!
english: We keep it real here, no faking it!
old: 'Raiz' = authentic/real. 'Frescura' = pretense/fussiness.
focus: One rule only: raiz is literally 'root' - rootsy/authentic, no frills; cut the second gloss (frescura).

target: Ela é show de bola, faz tudo direitinho.
english: She's awesome, she does everything just right.
old: 'Show de bola' = awesome/fantastic – informal expression.
focus: Literal hook: show de bola = 'a show of ball(-play)' - a football spectacle turned all-purpose praise.

target: Ele é muito pão-duro, nunca paga nada.
english: He's so stingy, he never pays for anything.
old: 'Pão-duro' = stingy person – common Brazilian expression.
focus: Literal hook: pao-duro is literally 'hard bread' = a tightwad.

target: Manda a real, você gostou ou não?
english: Tell me straight–did you like it or not?
old: 'Mandar a real' = to be honest/tell the truth – slang.
focus: Hook on mandar: literally 'send the real (one)' - mandar fronts many speech commands (manda ver).

target: Partiu praia no fim de semana?
english: Beach trip this weekend?
old: 'Partiu' + noun = 'let's go to' – very popular informal expression.
focus: Hook: partiu is literally past tense 'departed' - 'we're off' used to mean 'let's go'.

target: Ela deu conta do recado.
english: She got the job done.
old: 'Dar conta do recado' = to accomplish the task.
focus: Reusable chunk: dar conta de = to handle/manage; recado is the errand you deliver on.

target: Ela está com a corda toda hoje!
english: She's full of energy today!
old: 'Estar com a corda toda' = to be full of energy/enthusiastic.
focus: Literal hook: corda is a wind-up spring - com a corda toda = fully wound up.

target: Tu é ligeirão, hein? Resolveu tudo rapidinho.
english: You're quick, huh? Solved everything fast.
old: 'Ligeirão' = fast/quick person – informal.
focus: Grammar gem: the -ao augmentative - ligeiro (quick) + -ao = 'a real quick one'; works on many adjectives.

target: Ela é a menina dos olhos do pai.
english: She's the apple of her father's eye.
old: 'Menina dos olhos' = apple of one's eye.
focus: Fact hook: a menina dos olhos is literally the pupil of the eye - same image as English 'apple of the eye'.

target: Cara, essa festa vai ser irada!
english: Dude, this party is going to be awesome!
old: 'Cara' = dude. 'Irada' = awesome/sick – brazilian slang.
focus: One rule only: cara is literally 'face' - Brazil's all-purpose 'dude'; cut the second gloss (irada).

target: Tá osso conseguir emprego nessa cidade.
english: It's rough to get a job in this city.
old: 'Tá osso' = it's hard/difficult – informal expression.
focus: Literal hook: osso = 'bone' - ta osso = it's tough.

target: Pô, que vacilo! Esqueci a carteira em casa.
english: Man, what a blunder! I forgot my wallet at home.
old: 'Pô' = man/dude (exclamation). 'Vacilo' = mistake/blunder.
focus: One rule only: vacilo, from vacilar (cognate 'vacillate') - hesitation turned blunder; cut the Po gloss.

target: Ele está empurrando com a barriga.
english: He's being lazy.
old: 'Empurrar com a barriga' = to procrastinate/stall.
focus: Add the literal image: 'empurrar com a barriga' = pushing it along with your belly – shoving the task forward without doing it.

target: Ela está com o pé na jaca.
english: She's getting ahead of herself.
old: 'Estar com o pé na jaca' = to overdo it/go wild.
focus: Literal image – 'pé na jaca' = foot in the jackfruit; anchor the quoted chunk and land on 'went overboard'.

target: Ela tem o rei na barriga.
english: She's full of herself.
old: 'Ter o rei na barriga' = to be arrogant/self-important.
focus: Literal 'has the king in her belly' – as if pregnant with royalty; anchor 'o rei na barriga'.

target: Vou dar uma mãozinha para você.
english: I'll give you a hand.
old: 'Dar uma mãozinha' = to lend a hand/help out.
focus: Hook = the diminutive: 'mãozinha' is a little hand – the -inha softens the offer, a very Brazilian move.

target: Ele está com a corda no pescoço.
english: He's in a tight spot.
old: 'Estar com a corda no pescoço' = to be in financial trouble.
focus: Literal 'rope around the neck' plus the specific sense: money/debt pressure, not just any tight spot.

target: Ele está com o pé atrás em relação à proposta.
english: He's suspicious of the proposal.
old: 'Estar com o pé atrás' = to be wary/suspicious.
focus: Literal 'with one foot back' – ready to step away = wary; anchor 'pé atrás'.

target: Ela deu uma segurada no emprego.
english: She held on tight to her job.
old: 'Dar uma segurada' = to hold on/hold steady.
focus: The real insight is the productive pattern: dar uma + verb-ada = a quick, casual action (dar uma olhada, uma segurada).

target: Essa viagem foi tiro e queda.
english: This trip went off without a hitch.
old: 'Tiro e queda' = a sure bet/guaranteed success.
focus: Literal 'a shot and a fall' – one shot and the target drops = can't fail; anchor 'tiro e queda'.

target: Ele chutou o balde e pediu demissão.
english: He lost it and quit.
old: 'Chutar o balde' = to give up/throw caution to the wind.
focus: False friend with English 'kick the bucket': 'chutar o balde' means snapping / giving it all up, NOT dying.

target: Essa história tem muito mais pano pra manga.
english: There's a lot more to this story.
old: 'Pano pra manga' = material to work with/more to discuss.
focus: Literal 'cloth for a sleeve' – material left to work with; anchor 'pano pra manga'.

target: Ela deu com a língua nos dentes.
english: She let the cat out of the bag.
old: 'Dar com a língua nos dentes' = to spill a secret.
focus: Literal image – your tongue hits your teeth and the secret slips out; anchor 'língua nos dentes'.

target: A pessoa a quem me refiro não está presente.
english: The person I'm referring to is not present.
old: 'a quem' – preposition + 'quem' for people in relative clauses. The preposition must come before the relative pronoun.
focus: Hook = no preposition stranding: English says 'the person I'm referring TO', Portuguese must front it – 'a quem me refiro'.

target: O fato de ele ter se atrasado comprometeu toda a programação.
english: The fact that he was late compromised the entire schedule.
old: 'O fato de' + infinitive compound is common in complex clauses.
focus: English 'the fact THAT he was late' becomes an infinitive with its own subject: 'o fato de ele ter se atrasado' – that's the surprise.

target: A cidade que outrora fora próspera agora jazia em ruínas.
english: The city that had once been prosperous now lay in ruins.
old: The simple pluperfect (-ra ending) is literary – in speech, always use 'tinha + participle' instead.
focus: Quote the card: 'fora próspera' = had been prosperous; the -ra pluperfect is literary, speech says 'tinha sido'. Keep as the phenomenon's one telling.

target: Em que pese a oposição, o projeto seguiu adiante.
english: Notwithstanding the opposition, the project moved forward.
old: 'Em que pese' = 'despite/notwithstanding' – judicial/formal.
focus: Literal hook – pese is from pesar 'to weigh': roughly 'however it may weigh', a frozen legal formula for despite.

target: Se eu obtiver a aprovação, começo na semana que vem.
english: If I get approval, I start next week.
old: 'Obtiver' is the future subjunctive of 'obter'.
focus: Make this the future-subjunctive telling (stamps dropped elsewhere): after 'se' Portuguese uses a special future subjunctive – 'Se eu obtiver' = if I get. No paradigm table.

target: Em boca fechada não entra mosca.
english: In a closed mouth, no flies enter.
old: Literally 'a fly doesn't enter a closed mouth' – know when to stay quiet.
focus: Quote the target ('boca fechada') – the English field already gives the literal, so supply the point: keep quiet and you stay out of trouble.

target: Faz-se mister uma abordagem interdisciplinar.
english: An interdisciplinary approach is required.
old: 'Faz-se mister' = it is necessary – highly formal academic expression.
focus: 'mister' here means 'necessary' (nothing to do with English 'mister') – archaic legalese; anchor 'Faz-se mister'.

target: Quem não cola não sai da escola.
english: Those who don't cheat don't make it through school.
old: Humorous proverb – reflects a cultural observation, not a recommendation.
focus: Hook = 'cola': colar, literally 'to glue', is school slang for cheating – a cola is a crib sheet.

target: Quem com os porcos se mistura, farelo come.
english: Whoever associates with pigs will eat bran.
old: You become like the company you keep.
focus: Quote 'porcos' or 'farelo' – hang around pigs and you'll end up eating bran: bad company rubs off.

target: Gato escaldado tem medo de água fria.
english: A scalded cat fears cold water.
old: Literally 'a scalded cat is afraid of cold water'.
focus: The English field already IS the literal – give the meaning instead: once bitten, twice shy; quote 'gato escaldado'.

target: Sem embargo de toda a polêmica, o projeto foi adiante.
english: Notwithstanding all the controversy, the project went ahead.
old: 'Sem embargo de' = notwithstanding – formal/legal.
focus: Hook the false friend: 'embargo' here is not a trade ban – 'sem embargo de' is a formal/legal connective meaning 'notwithstanding'; quote the card's phrase.

target: Em sendo assim, não há mais o que discutir.
english: That being the case, there's nothing more to discuss.
old: 'Em sendo assim' – formal gerund construction.
focus: Explain the em + gerund pattern in plain words: 'em sendo assim' is literally 'in being so' – a formal construction English never builds; drop the bare jargon label.

target: O sertão vai virar mar, e o mar vai virar sertão.
english: The backlands will become sea, and the sea will become backlands.
old: Famous prophecy attributed to Antônio Conselheiro – about transformation.
focus: Anchor the culture in the language: this is Antonio Conselheiro's famous sertao/mar prophecy, and 'virar' = 'to turn into' is the everyday become-verb doing the transforming; cut the empty 'about transformation'.

target: O baião de Gonzagão é patrimônio cultural brasileiro.
english: Gonzagão's baião is Brazilian cultural heritage.
old: Luiz Gonzaga ('Gonzagão') is the king of baião music.
focus: The grammar is the -ao augmentative on a name: Gonzaga -> Gonzagao = 'big Gonzaga', affectionate size-upgrade Portuguese applies to people; keep one clause of who he is, teach the suffix.

target: Far-se-á necessária uma revisão completa do sistema.
english: A complete review of the system will be necessary.
old: Mesoclisis with 'se': far-se-á – literary future with reflexive pronoun.
focus: Lead with the surprise, not the term 'mesoclisis': in ultra-formal Portuguese the pronoun goes INSIDE the future verb – fazer + se + a = 'far-se-a'; written/legal only, nobody says this aloud.

target: Sem prejuízo das demais disposições, aplicam-se as seguintes normas.
english: Without prejudice to other provisions, the following rules apply.
old: 'Sem prejuízo de' – legal formula.
focus: Hook the false friend: 'prejuizo' normally means loss/harm, not prejudice (that's preconceito) – yet 'sem prejuizo de' is the exact legal calque of English 'without prejudice to'; quote the card.
